proposed_loop: THE UNIT OF THE LOOP: one advert -> one kit (tailored CV + letter) -> one status the user owns. The network is never required for any step; it only ever adds. THE ACCOUNT WALL, EXPLICITLY: today's gate is wrong twice over — it is on local-only code, and its copy (guest-invite.ts:138-147) says applications live in the account when applications-store.ts:2-9 says they are device-only. Move the wall from READING/WRITING to SYNCING. A signed-out person can: save an advert from the feed, paste an advert, tailor their CV, write or hand-draft the letter, export the letter PDF, and move it through all five statuses — on the phone, exactly as they can build and download a CV today. The account is asked for at the moment a server row becomes genuinely necessary: 'keep this on your account', 'follow it up', 'let Sumaiya remember it'. That is the same shape the CV path already proves works (local-owner.ts:124-157: guest rows are re-owned, keep their id, and are queued for upload), and it is the only placement consistent with the product's own non-negotiable. SCREEN BY SCREEN, PHONE FIRST. (1) BIRTH FROM THE FEED — jobs-screen.tsx JobCard (jobs-screen.tsx:75-85) gets a third action, 'Hifadhi kazi hii / Save this job', next to Tailor and Open the advert; job-detail-screen.tsx (footer at :48-61) gets 'Kuanza ombi / Start an application' that carries the WHOLE job object, not the sliced `jd` string it passes today (job-detail-screen.tsx:36-41). Both call createApplication with company/role/location/jobDescription/jobUrl and status 'saved'. No network, no account — the job is already in memory. (2) BIRTH FROM A PASTED ADVERT — keep the Applications empty-state 'Add a job' door (applications-screen.tsx:68-69) but frame it honestly as 'I have an advert that isn't in the feed'; the JD box on ApplicationDetail (application-detail-screen.tsx:176-184) plus a paste is the whole input, and the local matchJd fit score (application-detail-screen.tsx:53-56) already works with the network off. (3) BIRTH FROM THE TAILOR RESULT — this is the cheapest high-value fix: JobApply's result view (job-apply-screen.tsx:142-227) gains one button, 'Hifadhi hii kama ombi / Keep this as an application', which creates the Application with the JD it was given plus the cvId it used, and stores the letter it just produced. The screen that does the real work finally leaves a record. (4) THE WORKSPACE — ApplicationDetail becomes a three-part kit view: the advert (company, role, JD, applyUrl, and the closing date it already has on the job object), the kit (linked CV + the named letter PDF), and the status. Keep the five bilingual status chips exactly as they are (applications-store.ts:17-23, already correct and already translated) and add the one action that turns the loop: a primary 'Nimeomba / I applied' button that sets status=applied and stamps appliedAt — which createApplication/updateApplication already do (applications-store.ts:130,148) — then immediately offers the advert link and the letter download in the same breath, because that is the second the user is standing at the employer's form. (5) WHAT THE USER SEES PER STATUS — saved: 'you have this advert, your kit is ready'; applied: the date sent, a copy button for the letter, and the advert link; interview: the date and their notes (notesAlready exists, applications-store.ts:61) with the CV they sent one tap away; offer: the outcome, plus a prompt to log it so Sumaiya can learn from it; closed: kept, greyed, never deleted, so the history has a shape. The list keeps today's priority ordering (applications-store.ts:95-97) and gains an offline 'how it's going' strip: 'ulituma siku 7 zilizopita, hakuna jibu' — a local port of needsFollowUp/FOLLOW_UP_DAYS=7 (apps/web/lib/applications.ts:9,29), so the loop comes back to the user without a server call. (6) WHAT THE COVER LETTER IS — a real document from the same engine, not a field. Two halves, both required: OFFLINE, compose it from the JD + the linked CV and export through the path that already exists and already works (letterIsEmpty/letterToHtml at job-apply-screen.tsx:106,121 and services/pdf-export renamePdf at :127, with reportExport at :131) so the user gets a correctly named PDF with no data; SIGNED IN, 'Andika nami / Draft it with me' keeps calling the model but the returned body is STORED rather than kept in a textarea, and becomes the application's letter. Locally, replace the single `coverLetter` TEXT column with a small local letters table (id, applicationId, title, body, updatedAt) that mirrors web's cover_letter (schema.ts:75-81), so the second advert's letter doesn't overwrite the first and the web FK has somewhere to point later. (7) WHAT SYNCS — only when signed in AND online, through the queue that already exists: the application (id, company, role, location, jobDescription, jobUrl, cvId, status, fitScore, notes, createdAt, updatedAt, appliedAt) with the local `app-...` id sent as clientId for an idempotent upsert, exactly as createCV does today (use-offline-sync.ts:86, local-owner.ts:101); its letter; and its status transitions. Two new queue operations (create_application, update_application) join offline-storage's sync_queue (packages/utils/src/offline-storage.ts:103-107, consumed at use-offline-sync.ts:76-93), an owner column is added so claimGuestWork (local-owner.ts:124-157) can re-own applications on sign-in the way it re-owns CVs, and the 5-to-6 status map (saved->draft, interview->interviewing, closed->rejected|archived) lives in exactly one function. Server side that means extending the already-authenticated Hono /api/applications route (routes/applications.ts) with a clientId upsert and accepting the phone's statuses through that map — the surface is already mounted (app/api/[[...route]]/route.ts:88) and the web workspace, the dashboard grid, the brief, the application.followUp signal and the application.created outcome event all start working for phone users the moment rows land. Nothing syncs without an account, and nothing is lost by staying signed out.
instrumentation: application.created — fire where an Application is first written: the feed action (jobs-screen.tsx JobCard), the advert action (job-detail-screen.tsx:48-61), the pasted-advert door (applications-screen.tsx:68-69) and the tailor result (job-apply-screen.tsx:142-227). Props: via=feed|pasted|tailor, has_jd (bool), has_cv (bool), guest (bool). This is the event that answers 'does anyone start one, and from where'.

application_created — ALSO fire the already-declared funnel name FUNNEL_EVENTS.applicationCreated (apps/native/src/lib/analytics.ts:30) at the same four call sites. It is declared, it is already whitelisted by the admin aggregator (apps/web/lib/app-admin/aggregate.ts:12), and no call site has ever fired it; wiring it makes the native and web funnels comparable in one move.

application.status — fire in application-detail-screen.tsx save() only when the status actually changes (it currently does an unconditional update at :72). Props: from, to, via=form|applied_button. This is the single most valuable event in the whole domain: it is the only thing that proves the loop turns.

application.applied — fire at the new 'Nimeomba / I applied' primary action. Props: hours_since_created, had_letter (bool), had_tailored_cv (bool), guest (bool). Separates 'logged an advert' from 'actually applied'.

application.letter.drafted — on a successful draft, from application-detail-screen.tsx:122 (and from the JobApply letter path at job-apply-screen.tsx:57). Props: source=sumaiya|self, chars, offline (bool), guest (bool).

application.letter.draft_failed — on the catch at application-detail-screen.tsx:124-126. Props: reason=offline|auth|quota|error. This is the event that will prove or kill the claim that the account wall is what stops people: if reason auth is common, the wall is the cause; if it is rare, the missing feeder is.

application.letter.exported — fire beside the existing reportExport call (job-apply-screen.tsx:131, services/export-ledger.ts:35). Props: has_job_title (bool), guest (bool). It already has a server-side twin in download_log, so it is the one funnel step that can be verified from both ends.

application.deleted — fire in confirmDelete (application-detail-screen.tsx:83-96, delete at :92). Props: age_days, status. A high-signal negative: it says the record was not what the user wanted, and at which status they gave up.

applications.list.view — fire on useFocusEffect in the list (hooks/use-applications.ts:27-31, the hook that already fires on focus). Props: count, isEmpty (bool), guest (bool). This is the true top of the funnel and the denominator for every rate above.

applications.empty.cta — fire from the empty state's two doors (applications-screen.tsx:68-71). Props: action=find_jobs|add_job. Makes the two ways out of zero directly comparable, and will show whether 'Find jobs' dead-ends at the gate for guests.

job.detail.saved — fire from the new save action on job-detail-screen.tsx. Props: score (number|null), has_deadline (bool), source_name. Ties the feed's own match score to whether the advert was kept.

job.detail.apply_opened — fire in the existing outbound handler (job-detail-screen.tsx:55-58 and jobs-screen.tsx:141-143). Props: source_name, had_application (bool). The most important measurement in this domain: whether users finish the application on the employer's site (so the app is a preparation tool) or inside the app — that decides what the loop should optimise.

application.reminder.shown / application.reminder.tapped — fire from the new offline 'how it's going' strip on the applications list. Props: age_days, status. Measures whether the loop actually pulls people back without a server call.

application.claim.done — fire when guest applications are re-owned on sign-in, mirroring how CVs already prove the handoff (local-owner.ts:124-157). Props: claimed, failed. Tells you whether moving the wall to sync was safe in practice.

application.sync.failed — do NOT invent a new transport: route it through reportError({ scope: "applications.sync" }) so it lands in the existing app.error breadcrumb that is already wired to telemetry (apps/native/src/app/_layout.tsx:88-95). Props carried by the scope: op, retries.

Style rules to keep, all already enforced elsewhere: names fire from the screen that owns the action; props are counters, booleans and enums only; no content, no names, no phones (lib/telemetry.ts:9-17 rules 1-3 and the server-side sanitiser at routes/app-telemetry.ts:14-16, 100). Verification path if a row is ever in doubt: app_event stores props as jsonb via an explicit cast (app-telemetry.ts:100) specifically because a bare object double-encoded and made props->>'key' return NULL forever — so read the value back with props->>'via', never assume it landed.
